title: Preemptive scale-up lag causes tenant throttles; implement fallback preemption & headroom reconciliation
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: During a multi-tenant burst window on 2026-02-14 we observed sustained tenant throttling for two paying customers (AcmeHealth, NebulaPay). Symptoms: request queueing + 429s despite available overall GPU capacity. Investigation showed the autoscaler reliably detected load but its preemptive scale-up path was delayed due to leader election + backoff interplay, and the allocator did not opportunistically reclaim soft-reserved slots from idle warm pools. Result: reserved-pool shortfall and failed burst handoff for high-priority tenants.

This ticket tracks the diagnosis, hotfix PR, rollout plan, verification, and postmortem actions to prevent recurrence. It also contains customer comms and follow-ups for Dedicated capacity policy changes.
root_cause: A race in autoscaler leadership transition plus an exponential backoff misconfiguration caused the scale-up controller to postpone provisioning new instances by ~28–45s. Meanwhile the allocator's soft-reserve accounting did not allow preempting idle warm slots belonging to non-critical tenants because the soft-reserve reclaim path required a separate reconciliation cycle that runs every 60s. Combined, these timing paths created a window where high-priority tenants hit burst limits even though physical GPU capacity existed in the region.
mitigation:
1) Emergency patch deployed to reduce autoscaler leader-election backoff and to disable the long reconciliation delay for soft-reserve preemption (hotfix). 2) Temporary config: raised per-tenant burst credit to reduce immediate 429s for affected customers. 3) Applied transient routing fallback to safe-model variant for latency sensitive routes.

These mitigations were applied 2026-02-15 03:20 UTC and customer-facing mitigations rolled out within the same day.
proposed_fix:
Primary fix: implement direct soft-reserve reclaim in allocator that can be triggered synchronously by the autoscaler during scale-up (added RPC path). Adjust autoscaler backoff heuristics to base backoff on election duration observed in the last 10m window rather than a fixed doubling. Add a new sensor metric 'autoscaler.preempt_delay_seconds' and alerting when >10s for high-priority tenants.

Secondary: introduce tenant-priority preemption policy so high-priority tenants can reclaim warm slots from low-priority tenants during emergency bursts and add an opt-out flag for customers that must not be preempted.
implementation_notes:
- Code changes in repo infra/autoscaler: reduce default leader backoff from 8s->2s, add election-smoothed backoff algorithm.
- Code changes in repo infra/allocator: add ReclaimSoftReserve RPC + unit tests.
- Config change: soft_reserve_reconcile_interval from 60s -> 5s (temporary).
- Add feature flag 'soft_reclaim_sync' default off in staging; enable in canary region prior to global.
- Added integration tests simulating concurrent leader flips and tenant bursts.
comments: 2026-02-15 - Asha P.: Initial triage completed. Identified leader election/backoff + soft_reserve window as primary suspects. Notified Support and SRE; opened emergency patch PRs.

2026-02-15 - Marcus L.: Hotfix merged to canary; observed reduced preempt_delay_seconds from ~30s->6s in canary region. Customer throttles reduced for NebulaPay, AcmeHealth still saw intermittent 429s.
2026-02-20 - Maria Gomez (SRE): Canary rollout to us-east-1/2 completed. No regressions in perf tests. Starting staged rollout to eu-west-1.
2026-02-24 - Josh Kim (Product): Drafted customer postmortem and comms. Working with AcmeHealth SOC to confirm no data loss and provide SLA credit draft.
2026-03-03 - Eng Review: Request to add more conservative default for soft_reserve_reconcile_interval; changed to 15s in prod config and left 5s for emergency path behind feature flag.
2026-03-10 - Marcus L.: Code review complete. PRs awaiting ops runbook signoff and canary verification window closure.
verification_checks: No increase in 429s or tail latency for non-preempted tenants during synthetic burst tests
Heap/GC and pod churn in allocator remains within baseline after soft reclaim enabled
Monitor tenant burst success rate dashboard for top 10 paying customers for 48h post-rollout
rollback_plan: If we observe allocator instability or >5% increase in failed allocations within 30 minutes of rollout, flip feature flag 'soft_reclaim_sync' off and revert autoscaler backoff to previous value via config service. Ops will then execute controlled scale-up of reserved pools for affected tenants as an interim.
postmortem_actions: 1) Permanent change: implement synchronous reclaim + a safe preemption window; add opt-out knob for enterprise customers
2) Adjust autoscaler leader election tuning and add canary election tests into CI
3) Create a playbook for customer-facing mitigations and SLA credit calculations
4) Update Console: expose per-tenant preemption policy and historical preempt events
5) Run chaos tests that simulate leader flaps during heavy burst traffic
